comparison: Both evaluate claims C31, C38, C39, C40, C50 as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes immunoblotting data showing elevated RAPSYN in patient samples. Peer review notes all three reviewers accepted findings as 'convincing evidence' strengthened by primary sample data. Peer review additionally addresses C136 (correlation between RAPSYN and BCR-ABL), which OpenEval evaluates separately in R15.

Both address claims C36, C37 regarding mRNA levels. OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED based on RNA-seq and RT-PCR data indicating post-transcriptional regulation. Peer review marks as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 noting 'the disparity between RAPSYN protein and mRNA levels has not sufficiently been resolved' and recommending further discussion of the mechanistic explanation.

Both evaluate in vitro knockdown data (C42-C46, C51) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites comprehensive shRNA data across cell lines. Peer review includes these claims plus in vivo efficacy (C47-C49, C111), describing evidence as 'convincing' with adequate BCR-ABL-dependence controls. OpenEval evaluates in vivo claims separately in R4.

OpenEval R4 evaluates in vivo efficacy claims (C47-C49) as SUPPORTED with tumor growth inhibition and survival data. Peer review R3 includes these same in vivo claims alongside in vitro data, marking all as SUPPORTED. Both agree on the strength of in vivo evidence, though grouped differently.

OpenEval R5 addresses protein-protein interaction claims (C56-C58, C60) as SUPPORTED via co-IP and pull-down assays. Peer review R4 covers broader neddylation mechanism including these interaction claims plus C4, C5, C59, C61-C71, C74-C75, all marked SUPPORTED. Both agree on interaction data; peer review encompasses the full neddylation mechanism in one evaluation.

OpenEval R6 evaluates BCR-ABL neddylation claims (C5, C61-C71) as SUPPORTED with comprehensive evidence. Peer review R4 includes these claims within broader neddylation mechanism evaluation, describing findings from 'well-conducted in vitro experiments' and 'rigorous array of biochemical assays.' Both strongly support the neddylation mechanism.

OpenEval R7 addresses neddylation site identification (C74, C75) as SUPPORTED via LC-MS/MS and mutagenesis. Peer review R4 includes these claims in comprehensive neddylation mechanism evaluation, all marked SUPPORTED. Both accept the site identification data without challenge.

Both evaluate competition between neddylation and ubiquitination. OpenEval R8 addresses C6, C33, C76-C80 as SUPPORTED, showing inverse correlation and competitive effects. Peer review R5 includes these plus C81-C83, C137, describing mechanism as 'shielding BCR-ABL from ubiquitination through competition with c-CBL.' Both strongly support the competition mechanism.

OpenEval R9 evaluates c-CBL competition claims (C81-C83) as SUPPORTED via reciprocal co-IP experiments. Peer review R5 includes these claims within broader competition mechanism evaluation (also covering C6, C33, C76-C80, C137), all marked SUPPORTED. Both agree on competitive binding evidence.

Both evaluate SRC-mediated phosphorylation of RAPSYN (C7, C86-C90, C126) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites SRC inhibition, in vitro phosphorylation, and LC-MS/MS identification of Y336. Peer review confirms 'SRC-dependent phosphorylation facilitates NEDD8-ligase activity' and notes it 'deepens understanding of molecular interactions.' Both strongly support this mechanism.

Both evaluate phosphorylation effects on RAPSYN stability (C35, C91-C96) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval shows SRC inhibition accelerates RAPSYN degradation with rescue by MG132. Peer review R6 includes these claims in broader phosphorylation mechanism evaluation, confirming 'phosphorylation by SRC enhances RAPSYN stability.' Both agree on the link between phosphorylation and protein stability.

Both evaluate how SRC phosphorylation affects BCR-ABL neddylation (C34, C97-C102, C132) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval shows SRC inhibition reduces neddylation and Y336F abolishes this effect. Peer review R7 confirms 'SRC-dependent phosphorylation of RAPSYN facilitates its NEDD8-ligase activity.' Both strongly support this regulatory mechanism.

Both evaluate functional significance of Y336 phosphorylation (C8, C103-C110) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites rescue experiments showing RAPSNWT but not Y336F rescues shSRC toxicity and confers resistance. Peer review confirms 'physiological significance' through 'cell viability assays and in vivo models,' accepting rescue experiments without challenge. Both strongly support functional importance of Y336.

OpenEval R13 includes claims C8, C110 about Y336 functional effects. Peer review R7 addresses broader phosphorylation mechanism including these claims. Both mark as SUPPORTED, agreeing that Y336F mutant data demonstrates specificity of this phosphorylation site.

Both evaluate substrate specificity claims (C54, C72, C73) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes no change in AChR neddylation and no effect of AChR ligands on BCR-ABL. Peer review implicitly accepts these negative controls supporting specificity of RAPSYN's role in BCR-ABL versus canonical AChR function. Both agree on specificity in leukemia context.

OpenEval R15 evaluates correlation between RAPSYN and BCR-ABL (C136, C137) as SUPPORTED but notes mechanistic basis could be more explicit. Peer review R1 includes C136 in evaluation of co-expression data, marking as SUPPORTED without questioning the correlation. OpenEval is slightly more cautious about mechanistic interpretation.

OpenEval R15 addresses C137 (correlation between RAPSYN and BCR-ABL) as SUPPORTED but notes mechanistic basis needs clarification. Peer review R5 includes C137 in competition mechanism evaluation, marking as SUPPORTED. Both accept the correlation; OpenEval seeks more explicit mechanistic testing.

Both evaluate therapeutic specificity claims (C142, C146) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes C141 supported by minimal RAPSYN in healthy donors but C142 speculative without toxicity studies in normal cells. Peer review notes promising results but cautions about DepMap data showing no differential effects, concluding 'additional validation by future studies' needed. Both agree therapeutic window remains to be established.

OpenEval R17 evaluates combination therapy claims (C143, C144) as UNCERTAIN. C143 supported by increased saracatinib sensitivity with RAPSYN knockdown, but C144 speculative without testing in actual resistant cells. Peer review R8 includes C143 in functional significance evaluation marked SUPPORTED, accepting therapeutic implications. OpenEval is more cautious about extrapolation to resistance mechanisms.

Both evaluate PROTAC context claims (C9, C23) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are based on cited literature documenting PROTAC ineffectiveness, not original data. Peer review R11 accepts the cited literature and mechanistic explanation based on neddylation findings. Both agree these provide valid context for the study.

Both evaluate mechanistic explanation for PROTAC ineffectiveness (C114) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes neddylation competes with ubiquitination, providing mechanistic explanation, though direct PROTAC testing would strengthen conclusion. Peer review accepts this as 'reasonable inference from the data' that 'potentially uncovers avenues for targeted therapies.' Both support the inference while acknowledging it's not directly tested.

Both evaluate therapeutic targeting proposals (C121, C146) as UNCERTAIN/speculative. OpenEval notes these are 'reasonable hypothesis for future work rather than supported conclusion' without actual therapeutic development demonstrated. Peer review marks C146 as UNCERTAIN, noting promising results but requiring 'additional validation by future studies.' Both agree these are hypotheses requiring further validation.

OpenEval R21 evaluates tissue-specific regulation claims (C127, C131, C134) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are speculative inferences without experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims about differential phosphorylation contexts and PTM predictions.

Peer review R9 evaluates negative control experiments (C54, C72, C73) regarding AChR and specificity as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses these same claims in R14, also marking as SUPPORTED. This represents the same evaluation with different grouping.
